passages.quote: Liquid level measuring devices are classified into two groups: (a) direct method, and (b) inferred method.
In the gauge glass method, a transparent tube is attached to the bottom and top (top connection not needed in a tank open to atmosphere) of the tank that is monitored.
the liquid seeks its own level due to the pressure of the liquid in the vessel.
Gauge glasses made from tubular glass or plastic are used for service up to 450 psig and 400°F.
The presence or absence of liquid in the chamber determines if the light rays are refracted into the chamber or reflected back to the outer surface of the glass.
This causes the gauge glass to appear silvery-white.
This results in the glass appearing black
Light is bent, or refracted, to a greater extent in water than in steam.
The portion of the gauge containing water appears green; the portion of the gauge from that level upward appears red.
If the liquid level changes, the float will follow and change the position of the pointer attached to the rotating shaft.
The actual level range is determined by the length of the connecting arm.
The range of level measured will be limited only by the size of the vessel.
The magnetic bond method was developed to overcome the problems of cages and stuffing boxes.
When the liquid makes contact with any of the electrodes, an electric current will flow between the electrode and ground.
A typical system has three probes: a low level probe, a high level probe, and a high level alarm probe.
The relay in turn will actuate an alarm, a pump, a control valve, or all three.
The higher pressure, caused by the fluid in the tank, is compared to a lower reference pressure (usually atmospheric).
therefore, the pressure differential is the hydrostatic head, or weight, of the liquid in the tank.
The reference leg must be maintained dry so that there is no liquid head pressure on the low pressure side of the transmitter.
The gas or vapor pressure is equally applied to the low and high pressure sides.
To compensate for this effect, the reference leg is filled with the same fluid as the tank.
The ∆P transmitter is exposed to equal pressure on the high and low pressure sides when the liquid level is at its maximum; therefore, the differential pressure is zero.
the differential pressure and the transmitter output are inversely proportional to the tank level.
when differential pressure rises, indicated level rises for level detectors in a dry reference leg.

passages.quote: As the density of the steam or vapor increases, the weight increases and causes an increase in hydrostatic head even though the actual level of the tank has not changed.
As the temperature of the fluid in the tank is increased, the density of the fluid decreases.

some means of density compensation must be incorporated in order to have an accurate indication of tank level.

body.text: A dipstick is an example of the direct method. A pressure gauge at the bottom of a tank, reading hydrostatic head, is an example of the inferred method.

body.alt: Two tanks with transparent tubes beside them: one tube open at the top, and one connected to the tank at top and bottom.

body.text: Gauge glasses effectively form a U tube manometer, where
For higher temperatures and pressures, a metal-bodied gauge glass with a heavy glass or quartz section is used.

checks.q: What operating principle does a gauge glass use?
o: The liquid seeks its own level, like a U tube manometer
checks.x: Gauge glasses form a U tube manometer where the liquid seeks its own level.

checks.q: A pressure gauge at the bottom of a tank reads hydrostatic head. Which group of level measurement is this?
checks.x: A pressure gauge at the bottom of a tank is an example of the inferred method.

body.text: In a reflex gauge glass, light is reflected back at an air-glass interface.
Where water fills the chamber, the light is refracted into the chamber.

checks.q: In a refraction gauge glass, what color shows the portion containing water?
checks.x: The portion of the gauge containing water appears green, and from that level upward it appears red.

body.text: The ball float is a direct reading mechanism. A ball float is attached to a rod connected to a rotating shaft that indicates level on a calibrated scale.

body.alt: Ball float on a rod, connected through a stuffing box to a rotating shaft and pointer.
Chain float gauge: a float on a chain over a rotating element, with a weight keeping the chain taut.

body.text: A chain float is used where the small level limitations of ball floats must be exceeded.

body.alt: Magnetic float outside a non-magnetic tube, with an inner magnet connected to a level indicator.

body.text: The float travels outside a non-magnetic tube housing an inner magnet. The outer magnet attracts the inner magnet, which follows the level.
A float switch gives a simple, accurate, and reliable signal, such as to start a sump pump.

checks.q: What limits the level range of a ball float?
o: The length of the connecting arm
checks.x: The actual level range is determined by the length of the connecting arm.

checks.q: What limits the level range of a chain float?
checks.x: The range of level measured will be limited only by the size of the vessel.

checks.q: Why was the magnetic bond method developed?
o: To overcome the problems of cages and stuffing boxes
checks.x: The magnetic bond method was developed to overcome the problems of cages and stuffing boxes.

body.text: A conductivity probe system has one or more level detectors, an operating relay, and a controller.

body.alt: Conductivity probes of different lengths in a tank, connected to a controller.

body.text: The current energizes a relay, whose contacts open or close.

checks.q: In a conductivity probe system, what happens when liquid touches an electrode?
o: Current flows between the electrode and ground
checks.x: When the liquid contacts an electrode, an electric current flows between the electrode and ground.

concepts.title: Differential pressure: open tank and dry reference leg

body.alt: Open tank with a differential pressure detector on the bottom, and its low pressure side vented to atmosphere.

body.text: With an open tank, the low pressure side is vented to the atmosphere,
For a pressurized tank, both the high and low pressure sides must be connected.

body.alt: Closed tank with a high pressure connection below the liquid and a dry reference leg from the top of the tank to the low pressure side.

body.text: The transmitter output is therefore directly proportional to the hydrostatic head pressure, which is the level in the tank.

checks.q: Why must a dry reference leg be kept dry?
o: So there is no liquid head pressure on the low pressure side
To prevent corrosion of the tank
checks.x: The reference leg must be maintained dry so there is no liquid head pressure on the low pressure side.

checks.q: With a dry reference leg on a pressurized tank, why does gas pressure not affect the level reading?
o: It is much lower than the liquid head
It is applied equally to both sides of the transmitter
checks.x: The gas or vapor pressure is equally applied to the low and high pressure sides.

body.text: Where a tank contains a condensible fluid, condensation is greatly increased in the reference leg.

body.alt: Closed tank with a filled reference leg to the high pressure side and the tank connection to the low pressure side.

body.text: The filled leg applies a constant hydrostatic pressure to the high pressure side, equal to the maximum level to be measured.
A leak in the reference leg reduces differential pressure, causing indicated level to rise above actual level.

body.text: If a vapor with a significant density exists above the liquid, the hydrostatic pressure it adds needs to be considered.
The mass in the tank stays the same, but the density changes while the reference leg density stays about constant.

Calibration charts are also available to correct indications for changes in reference leg temperature.

checks.q: Why is density compensation needed in level detection?
o: Fluid density changes while reference leg density stays relatively constant
checks.x: If the tank fluid changes temperature and density, compensation is needed for an accurate indication.

checks.q: Which is one way density compensation is accomplished?
checks.x: Density compensation may be accomplished by electronic circuitry, pressure detector input, or instrument calibration.

checks.q: Which is one of the three reasons for using remote level indicators?
o: The level being measured may be in an unsafe/radioactive area
checks.x: The three reasons are distance from the facility, distance from the point of control, and an unsafe or radioactive area.

checks.q: In a D/P level instrument, what converts diaphragm motion into an electrical signal?
checks.x: The transducer changes this mechanical motion into an electrical signal.

checks.q: What are the three environmental concerns for level detection instrumentation?
o: Fluid density, ambient temperature, and humidity
checks.x: Density of the fluid, ambient temperature, and humidity can affect accuracy and reliability.

examples.problem: A wet reference leg develops a leak. What happens to indicated level compared with actual level?
steps: The leak reduces the liquid height on the high side
On a wet leg, falling differential pressure raises indication
examples.answer: Indicated level rises above actual level.
examples.cite: Word: Level Detectors.docx, slide 1.9 Your turn to practice!!

examples.title: Wet leg at maximum level
examples.problem: A wet reference leg tank is at maximum level. What differential pressure does the transmitter see?
steps: The reference leg head equals the maximum level
The two sides see equal pressure

facts.q: What are the two groups of level measuring devices?
How is differential pressure related to level with a wet reference leg?
facts.a: They are inversely proportional. Differential pressure is zero at maximum level.

facts.q: How is differential pressure related to level with a dry reference leg?
facts.a: Directly. Rising differential pressure means rising indicated level.

facts.q: What are the three methods of density compensation in level detection?
facts.a: Electronic circuitry, pressure detector input, and instrument calibration.

facts.q: What are the three reasons for remote level indication?
facts.a: Locations far from the main facility, a level far from the point of control, and an unsafe or radioactive area.

summary.text: Level instruments include the gauge glass, ball float, chain float, magnetic bond, conductivity probe, and differential pressure detector.
If a vapor with a significant density exists above the liquid, its hydrostatic pressure may need to be considered.
There are three major reasons for utilizing remote level indication.
Density of the fluid, ambient temperature changes, and humidity can affect level detection instrumentation.
